寄.meaning: On a dark night, something <part>strange</part> glows on your <part>roof</part>: a little green light, humming to itself. Every cat in the street creeps closer, then closer still, whiskers trembling. They just can't help but <kanji>draw near</kanji>.
寄.on: It's a lost brass <sound>key</sound>, floating and glowing, and the cats want to know which door it opens.
寄.kun: On their way home they stop in at your kitchen for a lick of <sound>yo</sound>gurt.

極.meaning: A <part>vise</part> clamps a <part>tree</part> and squeezes it tighter and tighter until its rings pop and sap squirts out like toothpaste. Bolts groan, the workbench bends, the floor cracks. This is squeezing taken to the <kanji>extreme</kanji>.
極.on: The sap oozes down the bench like a stic<sound>ky</sound> <sound>yolk</sound>.
極.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird hops onto the handle and cranks it one last notch: '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

異.meaning: Above a <part>rice field</part>, the scarecrows stand <part>together</part> in neat rows: identical straw hats, identical frowns. But one of them wears a pink tutu and is doing a handstand. Now that's <kanji>uncommon</kanji>.
異.on: Even odder, an <sound>ee</sound>l is wrapped round its ankle like a sock.
異.kun: At night it sleeps on a <sound>co</sound>t on <sound>to</sound>p of the barn, not out in the field like all the rest.

説.meaning: A little horned <part>imp</part> climbs onto an upturned bucket and gives a long <part>speech</part> about why socks should be worn on the ears. Nobody asked, and he won't stop. Well, everyone's entitled to an <kanji>opinion</kanji>.
説.on: His only fan is a red <sound>set</sound>ter, wagging its tail with a sock on each ear.
説.kun: He climbs to the <sound>to</sound>p of the bucket and explains it all over again, louder.

製.meaning: A clanking factory <part>system</part> of belts and blades swallows bolts of cloth at one end and spits out a finished <part>garment</part> every second. Each one gets the same little label sewn into the collar: <kanji>made in...</kanji> and the factory's name.
製.on: The finished shirts are locked in a huge steel <sound>sa</sound>fe until the trucks arrive.

花.meaning: A plain tuft of <part>grass</part> is tired of being stepped on, so one night it decides to <part>change</part>. It wriggles, stretches, and by morning a ring of bright yellow petals has burst out of its head. It's a <kanji>flower</kanji>.
花.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the pond next to it, just to get a sniff.
花.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs a passing bee, landing on it with a crumb of <sound>na</sound>an for a picnic.

増.meaning: The mole's hill was <part>formerly</part> one pinch of <part>soil</part>. Every night he adds another spadeful, and it grows to a hill, then a mountain, then a peak with snow on top. Every morning, watch it <kanji>increase</kanji>.
増.on: At the summit he paints a huge <sound>zo</sound>diac wheel round his telescope, sign after sign.
増.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, it's getting bigger!' he shouts down to his mother.

減.meaning: A <part>drill sergeant</part> orders his soldiers to drink up the <part>water drops</part> in the camp barrel. Gulp by gulp it empties, down to a puddle, then a drip, then a damp spot. The camp's supply starts to <kanji>dwindle</kanji>.
減.on: Then a bi<sound>g</sound> <sound>en</sound>gine pump gurgles up the very last drop.
減.kun: A thirsty <sound>he</sound>n pecks at the damp mud where the puddle used to be.

守.meaning: A grumpy grandma sits on the <part>roof</part> all night swinging a <part>golf club</part>, ready to bonk any burglar who climbs the drainpipe. Not one gets past her. She's the house's toughest <kanji>guard</kanji>.
守.on: She stays awake by crunching <sound>su</sound>gar cubes from her apron pocket.
守.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, we'll <sound>mo</sound>p the drainpipe with grease so nobody can climb it!' shout her grandkids.

確.meaning: Before you hang a <part>birdhouse</part>, you tie a heavy <part>stone</part> to it and let it swing all night in the storm. In the morning it's still there, not a nail loose. Now the birds can move in with total <kanji>assurance</kanji>.
確.on: Underneath it lies only a picked-clean fish <sound>carc</sound>ass that a crow dropped.
確.kun: To be extra sure, you throw a <sound>ta</sound>co at it, then duck behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld in case it bounces back.

裏.meaning: A farmer turns his old <part>garment</part> inside out and finds a whole tiny <part>farm</part> stitched into the lining: cows, barns and a duck pond. Nobody ever sees it from the front. All the best work is on the <kanji>back</kanji>.
裏.on: Further round, there's even a coral <sound>ree</sound>f embroidered in blue.
裏.kun: Hidden in the lining too: a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don and a tiny flag that says '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

低.meaning: Every member of the <part>clan</part> hangs a hat on the family <part>coat hook</part>, but it's too high for Grandpa. So they nail <part>one</part> plank to the wall underneath and move the hook down there. Now it's just right, a little <kanji>lower</kanji>.
低.on: Nobody can find a hammer, so they fix the plank up with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
低.kun: Grandpa clicks his <sound>hee</sound>ls, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of a clock hung at knee height.

積.meaning: A farmer pours <part>grain</part> into his silo until it overflows, then puts the <part>blame</part> on the silo for being too small. An inspector arrives with a tape measure: height, width, depth. He's checking the silo's <kanji>volume</kanji>.
積.on: He draws a pie chart, and spilled grain fills one big <sound>sec</sound>tor of it.
積.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the farmer, as the dusty grain piles up higher and higher.

留.meaning: A cowboy tries to leave through the <part>saloon doors</part>, but the sheriff points at the <part>rice field</part> outside: 'Nobody leaves till the harvest's in.' He's stuck pulling weeds for a week. The town will <kanji>detain</kanji> him.
留.on: His whole family turns up to help, and it becomes a muddy <sound>reu</sound>nion in the paddy.
留.kun: He stops dead at the <sound>to</sound>p of the saloon steps when he sees how big the field is.

題.meaning: The teacher sets a <part>rubber duck</part> on the desk, angled <part>just so</part>, and folds her arms. 'Today each of you will speak for five minutes about this.' The class groans. The duck is the <kanji>topic</kanji>.
題.on: To choose who goes first, she rolls a pair of <sound>di</sound>ce shaped like little ducks.

以.meaning: A <part>person</part> rushes in late for work again, holding up a <part>pole</part> with a single <part>dot</part> of mud on it as proof. 'I tripped over this! I'm only late <kanji>because</kanji> of a stick!'
以.on: 'And an <sound>ee</sound>l was wrapped round it,' he adds, out of breath.
以.kun: His <sound>mot</sound>to: by means of a good excuse, any lateness can be forgiven.

細.meaning: A tiny spider stitches a <part>rice field</part> with a single <part>thread</part> of silk, each square no bigger than a fingernail, each rice stalk a hair. Then she sets out a thimble teacup on top. Everything about her is <kanji>dainty</kanji>.
細.on: The thimble teacup holds one drop of apple <sound>ci</sound>der.
細.kun: She naps on a <sound>co</sound>t of moss while her <sound>ma</sound>ma checks every tiny, detailed stitch.

太.meaning: A <part>large</part> man eats one more <part>dot</part> of chocolate, just one, and snap! His belt gives way. He pats his round tummy happily and asks for seconds anyway. He's gone a bit <kanji>plump</kanji>.
太.on: He loosens his <sound>tie</sound> too and orders the dessert menu.
太.kun: He flops onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton and balances a cake on <sound>to</sound>p of his thick belly.

読.meaning: A market trader wants to <part>sell</part> his books, but nobody stops. So he opens one and turns every page into <part>speech</part>, voices and all. A crowd gathers, gasping at the plot. He doesn't just sell stories; he loves to <kanji>read</kanji>.
読.on: He moves his stall down to the <sound>dock</sound>, so the sailors can listen too.
読.kun: He reads aloud so long that his pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt goes warm in the sun.

星.meaning: A tiny <part>sun</part> has sprouted from a seed in your garden, full of <part>life</part>, growing leaves and humming. At night you pick it and toss it up into the sky, where it twinkles forever. You've planted a <kanji>star</kanji>.
星.on: You keep the next seed locked away in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe, just in case.
星.kun: It glows so <sound>ho</sound>t you have to catch it on a <sound>shi</sound>eld.

黒.meaning: The whole <part>farm</part> holds a sausage barbecue over a mountain of <part>hot coals</part>, but the farmer falls asleep. When he wakes up, the sausages, the cows, the fence and his own beard are covered in soot. Everything is <kanji>black</kanji>.
黒.on: A white <sound>cock</sound>atoo lands on the grill and flies off a sooty black one.
黒.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo sits on a <sound>ro</sound>ck nearby, black from beak to tail.

負.meaning: At the beach, a <part>shellfish</part> challenges you to a throwing contest. You fling your <part>boomerang</part> with all your might; it loops round and bonks you on the head. The shellfish wins by a mile. Total <kanji>defeat</kanji>.
負.on: You limp home and hide under your <sound>fu</sound>ton for the rest of the day.
負.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, I lost to a shellfish!' you wail from under the covers.

殺.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> finds a poison vine strangling her favourite <part>tree</part>. She grabs her <part>scissors</part> and snips through every stem until it shrivels and drops. That vine won't grow back: she's gone in for the <kanji>kill</kanji>.
殺.on: Then she rewards the tree with a juicy <sound>sats</sound>uma tied to its lowest branch.
殺.kun: She drags the dead vine off on a <sound>co</sound>t and buries it under a <sound>ro</sound>ck.

技.meaning: A sailor balances a heavy <part>anchor</part> on the tip of a thin <part>branch</part>, then spins it like a plate on a stick, and the twig doesn't even bend. The crowd on the pier roars. That takes real <kanji>skill</kanji>.
技.on: For an encore he does the same trick with a huge iron <sound>gea</sound>r.
技.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' gasp the shoppers in the ba<sound>za</sound>ar behind the pier.

由.meaning: A <part>pole</part> pokes up out of the top of the <part>sun</part>, like the stalk on an apple. Scientists gather and scratch their heads: who stuck it there? An old professor reads from a dusty book, but even he can't find the <kanji>wherefore</kanji>.
由.on: Then a <sound>u</sound>nicorn trots past, and they all suspect its horn was the reason.
由.kun: The unicorn licks a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt and hides behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld, saying nothing.

造.meaning: A boss stands at the top of a <part>ramp</part> and starts to <part>tell</part> her workers what she wants: 'A roller coaster! A water slide! A tower of jelly!' Each order rolls down the ramp and, clank, appears at the bottom. She loves to <kanji>create</kanji>.
造.on: Last of all, a giant spinning <sound>zo</sound>diac wheel rolls down and lands at her feet.
造.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock tumbles down the ramp too.

装.meaning: A <part>robust</part> wrestler squeezes into a sparkly <part>garment</part> two sizes too small, then adds a feather boa and a crown. Seams pop, sequins fly. He's off to the ball in his very finest <kanji>attire</kanji>.
装.on: First he scrubs his face with a whole bar of <sound>soa</sound>p.
装.kun: Then he spills <sound>yo</sound>gurt on one <sound>so</sound>ck and gasps '<sound>Oh</sound>!' as he dresses up.

適.meaning: A shopkeeper rolls a <part>hanging lantern</part> up a <part>ramp</part> to the front door and tries it on every hook. Too high, too low, too wobbly... the fourth hook holds it exactly, and it glows. That spot is perfectly <kanji>suitable</kanji>.
適.on: He sends his wife a <sound>tex</sound>t message: 'Found the spot!'
適.kun: She replies with a photo of a <sound>ca</sound>rp eating <sound>na</sound>an: her wish has come true.

望.meaning: Next to an old <part>tombstone</part>, a little <part>king</part> stands on tiptoe and stretches up toward the <part>moon</part>. His kingdom is one field and a gravestone, but he dreams of ruling the whole night sky. That's some <kanji>ambition</kanji>.
望.on: He tries to reach it by climbing to the top of a huge <sound>bou</sound>lder.
望.kun: '<sound>No</sound>t yet,' he tells a <sound>zo</sound>mbie rising from the tomb. 'I want the moon first.'

絶.meaning: A <part>hermit crab</part> has been knitting a scarf for ten years from one long <part>thread</part>. One day it snips the thread, puts down its needles and walks off the beach. No more scarf, ever. It's decided to <kanji>discontinue</kanji>.
絶.on: A pinch of lemon <sound>ze</sound>st in the sea breeze makes it sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
絶.kun: It spends the leftover wool money on a <sound>ta</sound>co instead.
